chunk_findings.detail:
The refusal path emits the *success* event kind with an empty sha: `promote_deployed` returns `O.refused("deploy.recorded", str(exc), env=env, sha="")`, i.e. the same `deploy.recorded` event that the happy path produces (`O.ok("deploy.recorded", **out)`). The reducer `_h_deploy_recorded` applies any event of that kind unconditionally, with no check that the event is a success or that `sha` is non-empty:

```python
st.deployments[ev.data.get("env", ev.subject)] = {
    "sha": ev.data.get("sha", ""), "at": ev.ts, "agent": ev.agent,
}
```

So a refused call that carries `env=<real env>, sha=""` overwrites a real deployment with an empty sha rather than being a no-op. Concrete sequence: production is live at `abc123` (recorded by an earlier successful hook), then a later hook call is refused — e.g. `ddflow promote deployed production --sha <bad>` (rejected by `PM.deployed`) or `ddflow promote deployed production` when production's branch cannot be resolved so `PromotionError` is raised. The `deploy.recorded` event with `sha=""` is applied, `state.deployments["production"]` becomes `{"sha": "", ...}`, and `promote status` afterwards reports no/blank `live <sha>` for production and treats the entire branch as undeployed — the exact opposite of the "what is live answered exactly" guarantee this change is for. The reducer cannot distinguish the refusal from a success because both use the same kind and the refusal payload deliberately mirrors the success payload; the refusal should either use a distinct kind or the reducer must ignore empty/refused `deploy.recorded` events.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/flow.py:promote_deployed → ddflow/core/model.py:_h_deploy_recorded

chunk_findings.detail: `W.git(repo, "rev-list", "--count", f"{live}..{head}")` returns `stdout` verbatim, which for `git rev-list --count` is `"<n>\n"` (a trailing newline is always emitted). `r.out.isdigit()` is therefore `False` on the success path, so `undeployed` stays `-1`. Demonstrated input: env `prod` with branch head `abcdef` (head) and `st.deployments["prod"]["sha"] == "abc123"` where `abc123` is 5 commits behind `abcdef`. The command prints `5\n`, `.isdigit()` is `False`, `undeployed == -1`, and `flow.py`'s `(n > 0)` test suppresses the suffix, so status shows `live abc123` with no undeployed count even though 5 commits are not deployed. The fix is to strip before the digit test, e.g. `s = r.out.strip(); undeployed = int(s) if r.ok and s.isdigit() else -1`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/promotions.py:122 (`promotions.status`, the `undeployed = int(r.out) ...` line)

chunk_findings.detail:
The rewritten description flattens the `toml` fragment example from a multi-line block
(`e.g.\n  [gate.unit_tests]\n  command = "pytest -q -n auto"`) to a single inline string:
`toml APPENDS a fragment such as [gate.unit_tests] command = "pytest -q -n auto" (needs
pytest-xdist).` Since `toml` appends the given text verbatim into `.ddflow/config.toml`, a
caller (e.g. an LLM following this description) that passes the example as written produces
the line `[gate.unit_tests] command = "pytest -q -n auto"`, which is not valid TOML: a table
header must be terminated by a newline before its keys. The previous description encoded the
required newlines (`\n`) so the example was copy-safe; the new one is not, so the documented
"such as" input yields a malformed config fragment when appended. (The same edit also silently
drops the `drop -n auto without it` caveat, but the loss of the embedded newlines is the part
that makes the shown input wrong.)
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/mcp.py:1847 (`ddflow_configure` description)

chunk_findings.detail:
`rev-list --count` writes the count followed by a newline; unless the `W.git` wrapper strips stdout, `r.out` is `"3
"`. Python's `str.isdigit()` returns `False` for `"3
"` (unlike `int("3
")`, which happily returns `3`), so the guard rejects every valid count and `undeployed` stays `-1`. The pipeline in `flow.py` then suppresses the annotation entirely (`f" ({n} undeployed)" if n > 0 else ""`), so with input such as an env that has 3 commits merged past the deployed sha, `promote status` prints only `live <sha>` and never reports the drift that this change exists to surface. The guard should strip before testing (`r.out.strip().isdigit()`), or just attempt `int(r.out)` and catch `ValueError`.
